newsitem.title: BRAZIL: U.S. says Chile's entry in NAFTA a 'priority'.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Chile's entry in NAFTA a 'priority'.

text.p: A top aide to U.S. President Bill Clinton said Chile's entry into the North American Free Trade Agreement was a priority and the White House was seeking speedy congressional approval for its inclusion in the pact.

White House Senior Counselor Thomas McLarty refused to speculate how quickly Congress would move to grant fast-track approval to make Chile a NAFTA member, but added: "We would hope to move forward in a very timely manner.
"This is a priority for our administration and we will be seeking consulations with Congress," McLarty told a news conference.

NAFTA, a free-trade agreement among the United States, Canada and Mexico, was signed early in the Clinton administration following several years of negotiations begun during the administration of former U.S. President George Bush.

Chile was earmarked by the Bush administration as the next likely NAFTA member, but attempts to include Chile have been stymied by congressional opposition and negative fallout from the Mexican financial crisis that erupted in late 1994.

McLarty, however, said the outlook for Chile's membership in the not-too-distant future was promising. He said that today there is a "general sense of promise and optimism" in the United States about Latin America.
He praised Chile's emerging democracy and said the nation had made great strides in improving socio-economic conditions for Chileans.
"They have moved to democracy, the elections were free and fair," he said, adding that a large part of Chile's federal budget is devoted to social programs.
McLarty is on the first leg of a three-nation tour of Latin America that will also take him to Argentina and Uruguay.
